title: Slicing Strings
description: Grab a single letter or a whole section out of a string.

content.value: Just like a list, a string has positions that start at index 0. You can grab a single letter by its index, the same way you grab an item from a list.

word = "Python"
print(word[0])  # Prints P
print(word[2])  # Prints t

To grab a section of a string instead of a single letter, use slicing. You write the start index, a colon `:`, and the end index. Python gives you the letters from the start index up to (but not including) the end index.

word = "Python"
# From index 0 up to (but not including) index 2:
print(word[0:2])  # Prints Py

If you leave out the first number, Python starts at the beginning: `[:3]` goes from the start to index 3. If you leave out the second number, Python goes all the way to the end: `[2:]` goes from index 2 to the end.

word = "Python"
print(word[:2])  # Prints Py
print(word[2:])  # Prints thon

quiz.question: If word = 'Magic', what does word[0] print?
quiz.explain: Counting starts at 0, so word[0] is the very first letter, 'M' in 'Magic'.

quiz.question: For word = 'Python', what does word[:2] print?
quiz.explain: `[:2]` means 'from the start up to (but not including) index 2', giving the first two letters: 'Py'.
